chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If an animal balks for one of you, meaning it stands in the land of the enemy or in the Way of Allah, then let him slaughter it and not hamstring it.'

key_terms.حَرَنَتْ: The animal barks or refuses to move forward
key_terms.يُعَرْقِبْهَا: To hamstring it (cut the tendons of the legs)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughtering a horse or camel that refuses to move during battle?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the practical jurisprudence of jihad logistics, balancing the utility of the animal against the need to prevent enemy capture or hindrance. The prohibition of 'urqabah' (hamstringing) ensures the animal remains a viable resource for sustenance rather than becoming a useless burden, reflecting the Prophetic emphasis on efficient resource management during military campaigns. This specific instruction underscores the Shia tradition's attention to the nuanced legal details of warfare and animal welfare as derived directly from the Prophet (SAW).
